name: Character Body
description: The moving body itself: position, velocity, size, gravity, and the collision resolution that turns one into the other. Everything else in the side-view movement set sets a velocity and lets this integrate it. Resolution is axis-separated — horizontal first, then vertical — so a body sliding along a wall keeps its other axis instead of sticking, and a blocked axis zeroes only that component of velocity. Gravity lives here rather than on the jump, so a build with locomotion and no jump still falls; before this existed, gravity arrived with whichever component happened to declare movement.physics_core, which made falling depend on being able to jump. It emits nothing: movement.ground_sensor already announces landing and takeoff, and a body that reported the same contact again would be one fact with two sources.

inputs.name: width
inputs.description: Body width in world units. Narrower than a tile on a tile-based stage, so a one-tile gap is passable.

inputs.name: gravityScale
inputs.description: Multiplier on movement.physics_core's gravity, so one body can be floatier than another without changing the world constant every other component reads.

inputs.name: terminalFallSpeed
inputs.description: Downward speed cap. Without one, a long fall accumulates enough speed to tunnel through a thin floor between two frames.

inputs.name: maxRiseSpeed
inputs.description: Upward speed cap, so a stacked jump and knockback impulse cannot launch the body out of the world.

outputs.name: isBlockedHorizontally
outputs.description: The last horizontal move was stopped by a solid. Read it before blaming input handling for a character that will not move.
